learn.hook: Where does the water in your tap come from? Let's follow it back to where it started!
points: Rain is the main source of fresh water. Rainwater fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells.
Some rainwater soaks into the ground. We draw this groundwater using wells, hand pumps and borewells.
Snow on high mountains melts and flows into rivers. The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas.
Sea water is salty, so we cannot drink it or use it to water crops.
Long ago, people built stepwells (baoris or vavs) to store water, like the Rani ki Vav in Gujarat and Chand Baori in Rajasthan.

example.q: There is plenty of water in the sea. Why can't the people of Chennai simply drink sea water?
steps: Sea water tastes very salty.
Salty water is not safe for drinking.
So fresh water from rain, rivers, lakes and the ground is needed for drinking.
example.answer: Sea water is too salty to drink

learn.reallife: Find out where your home's water comes from — a river, a lake, a well or a borewell. Ask an elder!

games.title: Water place and where it is

quiz.q: What is the main source of fresh water on Earth?
quiz.explain: Rain fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells, and soaks into the ground.
steps: Rain fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells.
So rain is the main source of fresh water.
Answer: Rain
quiz.mistake: Thinks water starts in the tap

quiz.q: Why can we not drink sea water?
quiz.explain: Sea water has a lot of salt. Drinking it is harmful.
steps: Sea water has a lot of salt.
So it is too salty to drink.
Answer: It is too salty
quiz.mistake: Does not know sea water is salty

quiz.q: Where does the river Ganga begin?
quiz.explain: The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas in Uttarakhand.
steps: The Ganga starts in the Himalayas.
It begins at the Gangotri glacier.
So the answer is Gangotri glacier.
Answer: Gangotri glacier
quiz.mistake: Mixes up where a river starts and where it ends

quiz.q: Water found under the ground is called ___.
quiz.explain: Rainwater soaks into the soil and is stored under the ground as groundwater.
steps: Some rainwater soaks into the ground.
Water stored under the ground is groundwater.
So the answer is groundwater.
Answer: Groundwater
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word groundwater

quiz.q: Which of these takes water out from under the ground?
quiz.explain: Hand pumps and borewells pull up groundwater.
steps: We draw groundwater using wells, hand pumps and borewells.
So the hand pump takes water out from under the ground.
Answer: Hand pump
quiz.mistake: Does not know how groundwater is used

quiz.q: What is a stepwell?
options: An old well with steps going down to the water
quiz.explain: Stepwells have steps that lead down to the water. They were built to store water in dry areas.
steps: Long ago people built stepwells (baoris) to store water.
They have steps going down to the water.
So that is a stepwell.
Answer: An old well with steps going down to the water
quiz.mistake: Has never heard of stepwells

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a source of fresh water?
quiz.explain: The sea has salty water. Rivers, lakes and rain give fresh water.
steps: Rivers, lakes and rain give fresh water.
The sea has salty water.
So the sea is NOT a source of fresh water.
Answer: The sea
quiz.mistake: Thinks all water is fresh

quiz.q: Snow on mountains melts in summer. Where does this water go?
quiz.explain: Melting snow flows down as streams that join rivers.
steps: Snow on high mountains melts in summer.
It flows down into streams and rivers.
So that is where the water goes.
Answer: Into streams and rivers
quiz.mistake: Does not link melting snow with rivers

teach.ask: Gappu is thirsty and asks: where does all our water come from?
teach.praise: Tweet! Rain is the start of every river and well!
teach.nudge: Can we drink the salty sea water?

revise.summary: Rain is the main source of fresh water. It fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells and soaks into the ground as groundwater. Melting snow feeds rivers like the Ganga. Sea water is too salty to drink.
focus: Groundwater and how we draw it
remember: Rain = main source of fresh water
Groundwater is drawn by wells, hand pumps and borewells
The Ganga starts at the Gangotri glacier
Stepwells: Rani ki Vav (Gujarat), Chand Baori (Rajasthan)
traps: The sea is not a source of drinking water; it is salty.
Taps are not the source of water; they only bring it to us.

learn.hook: Count how many times you use water today. You may be surprised!
points: We need water to drink, cook, bathe, brush our teeth and wash clothes and dishes.
Farmers need water to grow crops. Plants cannot live without water.
Animals need water to drink, and fish and lotus live in water.
Boats carry people and goods on rivers and seas.
Drinking water must be clean. Boiling or filtering water makes it safe to drink.

example.q: Raju's family boils drinking water and lets it cool before drinking. Why?
steps: Water may look clean but can still have tiny germs.
Germs can make us sick with stomach problems.
Boiling kills these germs, so the water becomes safe.
example.answer: Boiling kills germs and makes the water safe to drink

learn.reallife: Keep your water bottle clean and covered. Drink water often, especially on hot days.

games.title: Who uses this water?
items: Buffaloes cooling off in a pond

items.q: Heat water till it bubbles to kill germs
It carries goods across a river
Bathe with a mug and a ___ to save water
It removes dirt from drinking water
Black animal that gives milk and loves to cool off in ponds

quiz.q: Which of these needs water?
quiz.explain: Rice is cooked in boiling water.
steps: We need water to drink, cook and bathe.
Rice is cooked in boiling water.
So cooking rice needs water.
Answer: Cooking rice
quiz.mistake: Does not notice everyday uses of water

quiz.q: Why do farmers need water?
quiz.explain: Crops need water to grow. Farmers get it from rain, rivers, wells and canals.
steps: Plants cannot live without water.
Farmers need water to grow crops.
So that is why farmers need water.
Answer: To grow crops
quiz.mistake: Does not link water with food

quiz.q: Which crop is usually grown in fields filled with water?
quiz.explain: Rice is often grown in fields covered with standing water.
steps: Rice is often grown in fields with standing water.
So the answer is rice.
Answer: Rice
quiz.mistake: Does not know that rice needs a lot of water

quiz.q: How can we make drinking water safe?
quiz.explain: Boiling kills germs and a filter removes dirt and germs.
steps: Drinking water must be clean.
Boiling or filtering makes it safe.
So boil it or filter it.
Answer: Boil it or filter it
quiz.mistake: Thinks clear-looking water is always safe

quiz.q: What can happen if we drink dirty water?
quiz.explain: Dirty water can have germs that cause illnesses like diarrhoea.
steps: Dirty water can have germs.
Germs can cause stomach illnesses.
So we can get stomach illnesses.
Answer: We can get stomach illnesses
quiz.mistake: Does not link dirty water with illness

quiz.q: How do boats help people?
options: They carry people and goods across water
quiz.explain: Boats travel on rivers, lakes and seas, carrying people and goods.
steps: Boats travel on rivers and seas.
They carry people and goods.
So that is how boats help.
Answer: They carry people and goods across water
quiz.mistake: Does not see water as a way to travel

quiz.q: Reena drinks 6 glasses of water every day. How many glasses does she drink in 2 days?
quiz.explain: 6 glasses each day for 2 days is 6 + 6 = 12 glasses.
steps: 6 glasses × 2 days
Answer: 12
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 2 instead of doubling

quiz.q: Why should we keep our drinking water covered?
options: To keep dust, flies and germs out
quiz.explain: Uncovered water can collect dust and germs from flies.
steps: Uncovered water can collect dust and germs from flies.
Covering keeps them out.
So keep drinking water covered.
Answer: To keep dust, flies and germs out
quiz.mistake: Does not know how water gets dirty

teach.ask: Gappu has a bowl of water and wonders what all it can be used for. Can you tell him?
teach.praise: Chirp! Water is used for almost everything!
teach.nudge: How do farmers and plants use water?

revise.summary: We use water to drink, cook, bathe and clean. Farmers need it for crops, animals need it to drink, and boats travel on it. Drinking water must be clean, covered, and boiled or filtered.
focus: Uses of water at home, on farms and for animals
remember: Rice is often grown in fields with standing water
Boiling or filtering makes water safe to drink
Dirty water can cause stomach illnesses
traps: Water that looks clear may still have germs; boil or filter it.

learn.hook: Fresh water is precious. Only a small part of all the water on Earth is fresh and fit to drink!
points: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water. Fresh water is limited, so we must not waste it.
Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth or soaping your hands.
Use a bucket and mug for bathing instead of letting water run.
Get leaking taps fixed. Reuse water used for washing vegetables to water plants.
Rainwater harvesting means collecting and storing rainwater for later use.

example.q: Aryan leaves the tap running while he brushes his teeth. What should he do, and why?
steps: Water flows away and is wasted while the tap runs.
He can fill a mug of water and turn the tap off.
This saves fresh water, which is limited.
example.answer: Turn off the tap while brushing and use a mug, to save water

learn.reallife: World Water Day is on 22 March. Make a 'Save Water' poster for your school that day!

games.title: Saving or wasting water?
items: Bathing with a bucket and mug
Leaving the tap on while brushing
Washing a car with a running pipe

games.title: Water-saving facts
items: Most of the water on Earth is salty.
Most of Earth's water is in the seas and oceans.
A dripping tap does not waste any water.
Drops add up to buckets of wasted water.
Rainwater harvesting means storing rainwater for later.
The stored water can be used or can refill groundwater.
World Water Day is on 22 March.
It reminds the whole world to save water.
Using a mug while brushing saves water.
A mug of water is enough, and the tap stays off.

quiz.q: Which habit saves water?
options: Turning off the tap while brushing
Bathing under a running pipe for an hour
quiz.explain: Turning the tap off when you are not using it stops water from going down the drain.
steps: We must not waste water.
Turning off the tap while brushing saves water.
So that habit saves water.
Answer: Turning off the tap while brushing
quiz.mistake: Does not notice small wastes of water

quiz.q: What is rainwater harvesting?
options: Collecting and storing rainwater for later use
quiz.explain: Rainwater from roofs can be collected in tanks or sent into the ground to refill groundwater.
steps: Rainwater harvesting means collecting rainwater.
It is stored for later use.
So that is rainwater harvesting.
Answer: Collecting and storing rainwater for later use
quiz.mistake: Thinks harvesting only means cutting crops

quiz.q: A tap leaks and wastes 1 bucket of water every day. How many buckets are wasted in a week?
quiz.explain: A week has 7 days. 1 bucket each day for 7 days is 7 buckets.
steps: 1 bucket each day
7 days in a week
Answer: 7
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a week has 7 days

quiz.q: Why should we save fresh water?
options: There is too much fresh water
Fresh water is limited and everyone needs it
quiz.explain: Most water on Earth is salty. Fresh water is limited, so we must not waste it.
steps: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water.
Fresh water is limited and everyone needs it.
So we should save it.
Answer: Fresh water is limited and everyone needs it
quiz.mistake: Thinks fresh water will never run out

quiz.q: How can water used for washing vegetables be reused?
quiz.explain: This water is fine for plants, but not for drinking or cooking.
steps: Water used for washing vegetables can be reused.
It is fine for watering plants, not for drinking or cooking.
So reuse it to water the plants.
Answer: To water the plants
quiz.mistake: Thinks reused water is fit for drinking

quiz.q: Which is a better way to bathe and save water?
options: Letting the shower run while playing
Keeping the pipe on all day
quiz.explain: A bucket bath uses a fixed amount of water and avoids waste.
steps: Letting water run wastes it.
A bucket and mug use a fixed amount.
So a bucket and mug is better.
Answer: Using a bucket and mug
quiz.mistake: Does not compare how much water each way uses

quiz.q: World Water Day is celebrated on ___.
quiz.explain: World Water Day is on 22 March. 5 June is World Environment Day.
steps: World Water Day is on 22 March.
5 June is World Environment Day.
So the answer is 22 March.
Answer: 22 March
quiz.mistake: Mixes up World Water Day and World Environment Day

quiz.q: You see a tap running in the school washroom with no one using it. What should you do?
options: Turn it off and tell a teacher if it is broken
quiz.explain: Turning off a running tap saves water. A broken tap should be reported so it can be fixed.
steps: A running tap wastes water.
Turn it off, and tell a teacher if it is broken so it gets fixed.
So that is what you should do.
Answer: Turn it off and tell a teacher if it is broken
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is someone else's job

teach.ask: Gappu sees a tap dripping all day. He asks: why should we save water, and how?
teach.praise: Tweet! I will close the tap and save every drop!
teach.nudge: Why can't we just use as much water as we like?

revise.summary: Fresh water is limited, so we must not waste it. Turn off taps, use a bucket and mug, fix leaks, reuse water for plants, and collect rainwater.
remember: Turn off the tap while brushing or soaping
Rainwater harvesting = collecting and storing rainwater
traps: Don't think there is plenty of fresh water; most water on Earth is salty.
Water from washing vegetables is for plants, not for drinking.
